finding.claim: DNS rebinding TOCTOU defeats the SSRF guard: _is_safe_url resolves the host at line 79, then requests re-resolves at line 83 with no IP pinning, so an attacker-controlled host can pass the check with a public IP and fetch from 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254.
finding.source: Chat completion request: image/video/audio http(s) URL with an attacker-controlled hostname (serve/processors/multimodal.py:162-184)
finding.sink: client.get(parsed.url) at lmdeploy/vl/media/connection.py:83 (outbound request to internal address)

trace.note: _is_safe_url resolves hostname via getaddrinfo, requires is_global on all results
requests.Session.get re-resolves hostname; resolved address not pinned
redirects are handled manually and re-checked, which is good, but does not close the rebinding gap

finding.guards_checked: _is_safe_url is_global check on all resolved IPs (connection.py:26-54); scheme check (:71); allowed_media_domains exact-hostname match when configured (:75); manual redirect re-validation (:85-90); consistent urllib3 parse_url on both sides. Default with no allowlist leaves the rebinding window open. Only GET, response parsed as image bytes, so exfiltration is limited to decodable responses; blind SSRF and host/port timing oracle remain. Confidence medium: requires attacker-controlled DNS with short TTL. Not run.
